item.description: Folklore and Mystery: Underneath Montana's Streets /sites/default/files/styles/400x500/public/public%3A/saloon.jpg?itok=waMWX2Za But Havre is not alone in having once had a secret life underground. item.title: Montana Glaciers From Above!
item.description: Montana Glaciers From Above! /sites/default/files/styles/400x500/public/public%3A/GlacierNP%20-%20Ahern%20Glacier_0.jpg?itok=MKh7MpE7 Aerial Photography of Glacier National Park Glaciers add a nuance of complexity to mountain flying. As it is, mountain flying is complicated and can be dangerous due to wind, terrain, altitude, reduced aircraft performance, turbulence, and weather.

item.title: BEYOND WORDS: C.M. Russell's Real Montana Winters
item.description: BEYOND WORDS: C.M. Russell's Real Montana Winters /sites/default/files/styles/400x500/public/public%3A/Jumped_0.jpg?itok=ZSSMVR_r The phrase "words can't describe it" is often used when a person is trying to articulate something either extremely good or extremely bad. And mere words definitely could not describe the extremely bad winter of 1886-87 for the Montanans who experienced it.

item.title: Ernest Hemingway’s Adventures in Montana
item.description: Ernest Hemingway’s Adventures in Montana /sites/default/files/styles/400x500/public/public%3A/EH5145P.jpg?itok=kP-xkB_a Hemingway’s time in the Yellowstone High Country began on July 13, 1930, when he first crossed the Clark’s Fork and settled onto the L—T Ranch ten miles outside of Cooke City, Montana. The ranch was owned by Olive and Lawrence Nordquist; the “L” and “T” stood for the first and last letters in the latter’s name.

item.title: Keeping Accounts: Ledger Artists Celebrate the Blackfeet in Montana
item.description: Keeping Accounts: Ledger Artists Celebrate the Blackfeet in Montana /sites/default/files/styles/400x500/public/public%3A/Black%20Horse%20Medicine.JPG?itok=cySVgaGl The Baker Massacre—what many Blackfeet call Bear River Massacre because they would rather not speak Baker’s name—is still too vivid and raw for Guardipee to paint. Pepion has never painted it either.

item.description: Top 9 Architectural Gems of the Treasure State /sites/default/files/styles/400x500/public/public%3A/Helena%20Cathedral.jpg?itok=jV0Pi1p1 The treasure state is aptly named, though it includes as many man-made treasures as natural wonders. item.title: Bouldering Montana: Five Spring Bouldering Spots
item.description: Bouldering Montana: Five Spring Bouldering Spots /sites/default/files/styles/400x500/public/public%3A/Lost%20Horse%20Kyle%20Redberg%202.jpg?itok=Y7zL_7bq There’s nothing like hauling your body up a slab of million-year-old gneiss to get your blood pumping. Come spring, the friction tends to be good and it’s sometimes even warm enough to climb in shirtsleeves. Bouldering is a stellar way to spend time outside with friends, explore the outer realms of your comfort zone, and build strength.

item.title: Get to Know a County: Sanders County
item.description: Get to Know a County: Sanders County /sites/default/files/styles/400x500/public/public%3A/Bighorn%20Sheep.jpg?itok=XZdRagmH Perhaps the most famous resident of Sanders County is David Thompson. Sent by the British Crown with the aim of beating Lewis and Clark to the Pacific, Thompson has been described as the most important geographer you’ve never heard of. item.title: Charlie Chaplin’s Butte, America
item.description: Charlie Chaplin’s Butte, America /sites/default/files/styles/400x500/public/public%3A/grand%20theater%2C%20formerly%20Maguire%20Opera%20House%20.jpg?itok=vEv3-Qzr Chaplin’s autobiography lingers on a particular stop along his tour, an American city which, even from the distance of a half a century on and a continent away, he was able to recall vividly: Butte, Montana.
